claim: Predeterminer modifiers are virtually incompatible with pronouns. The one exception is all with 1st and 2nd person plural pronouns followed by a modifier.
evidence_summary: §12, p. 433, gives “two very restricted cases”: all with we or you, and fractions and multipliers with a fused relative, as in I sold it for half/twice what I had paid.
finding: Add the second case to p. 430 or cross-refer to §12.
proposed_wording: The exceptions are all with 1st and 2nd person plural pronouns … and fractions or multipliers with fused relative what (§12).
inference: Is all + we/you the only predeterminer construction with a pronoun head?

evidence.passage: §10.2, p. 430. “The one exception is that all combines with the 1st and 2nd person plural pronouns”.
evidence.example: §12, p. 433, and its example with half/twice what I had paid.
evidence.establishes: Two inventories of the same exceptions differ.
evidence.note: Local source (working note, unpublished draft or local copy); not online.
